title: Why ATP works as money
endLine: ATP is cash, not savings: spent by work, remade by fuel.

scenes.tts: The first film showed A T P paying for glucose's uphill step. Now look at the wallet. Your body holds well under a kilogram of A T P at any moment. Yet you recycle roughly forty kilograms of it every day. How can so small a pool keep up?
scenes.caption: The first film showed ATP paying for glucose's uphill step. Now look at the wallet. Your body holds well under a kilogram of ATP at any moment. Yet you recycle roughly 40 kilograms of it every day. How can so small a pool keep up?
scenes.visual: Continue the first film's world and colour map without a reset: the broad GREY schematic hill fills about 70% of the frame height, tagged 'schematic' at bottom right all film. COLOUR BY CONCEPT, as in the first film: ATP, phosphoryl groups and activated carriers YELLOW; glucose and fuel carbon BLUE; favourable flow GREEN; heat and losses RED; enzymes and ordinary labels TEXT. New in this film: electrons are small TEAL sparks. Opening recap (first sentence): a faint ghost of the first film's joined carts crosses the crest, the YELLOW 'ATP' cart rolling down as the BLUE 'glucose' cart rises, then the ghost fades. On 'look at the wallet', a small open tray labelled 'ATP in body' sits on a ledge at mid-height on the hill, holding four YELLOW 'ATP' beads. On 'well under a kilogram', a tag under the tray reads 'under 1 kg'. On 'forty kilograms', a day counter at top right runs from 06:00 to 24:00 while YELLOW beads leave the tray downhill and new ones drop back in, a tally stack beside it growing to a tag 'about 40 kg a day'; the tray itself never grows. On the question, large white text across the top: 'How does a tiny pool keep up?' Bead traffic continues.
scenes.narration: The first film showed ATP paying for glucose's uphill step. Now look at the wallet. Your body holds well under a kilogram of ATP at any moment. Yet you recycle roughly 40 kilograms of it every day. How can so small a pool keep up?

scenes.visual: Keep the hill, tray and bead traffic moving dimly behind. Centre the title 'Why ATP works as money' for two seconds, then lift it away as the tray brightens.

scenes.tts: It keeps up because A T P is not stockpiled. Each molecule is spent and remade hundreds of times a day, like cash passing through your hands. That raises two questions. Why is A T P good money? And what keeps remaking it?
scenes.caption: It keeps up because ATP is not stockpiled. Each molecule is spent and remade hundreds of times a day, like cash passing through your hands. That raises two questions. Why is ATP good money? And what keeps remaking it?
scenes.visual: Zoom gently toward the tray. Follow one YELLOW 'ATP' bead: it rolls down the hill to a lower ledge, its label turns to 'ADP' and it dims, then an unlabelled lift on the hillside carries it back up to the tray where it brightens to 'ATP' again; a loop counter beside the tray ticks 1, 2, 3 and then spins up toward 'hundreds a day'. Other beads loop the same way behind it. On 'two questions', two white tags appear on either side of the loop: 'good money?' beside the tray, 'what remakes it?' beside the lift. Keep at most six objects on screen.
scenes.narration: It keeps up because ATP is not stockpiled. Each molecule is spent and remade hundreds of times a day, like cash passing through your hands. That raises two questions. Why is ATP good money? And what keeps remaking it?

scenes.tts: Start with the money. Rank phosphorylated compounds on a ladder by the free energy each releases, handing its phosphoryl group to water. Under standard conditions, transfers run downhill. A T P sits in the middle. Compounds above it can recharge A D P. A T P, in turn, phosphorylates compounds below it.
scenes.caption: Start with the money. Rank phosphorylated compounds on a ladder by the free energy each releases, handing its phosphoryl group to water. Under standard conditions, transfers run downhill. ATP sits in the middle. Compounds above it can recharge ADP. ATP, in turn, phosphorylates compounds below it.
scenes.visual: Transform the hillside, in place, into three broad terraces stacked like rungs: the vertical axis is tagged 'transfer potential (schematic)', with no numbers. The tray stays on the MIDDLE terrace, labelled 'ATP'. The TOP terrace holds two unnamed YELLOW-outlined blocks labelled only 'richer donors'; the BOTTOM terrace holds two unnamed BLUE blocks labelled only 'acceptors below'. Do not name or place any specific compound. On 'transfers run downhill', GOLD phosphoryl badges slide only downward along the terraces, never up. On 'recharge ADP', a badge drops from a top block into a dim 'ADP' bead on the middle terrace, which brightens to 'ATP'. On 'phosphorylates compounds below', a badge drops from the tray to a bottom block, which lights GREEN. The two downward drops repeat slowly as ambient motion.
scenes.narration: Start with the money. Rank phosphorylated compounds on a ladder by the free energy each releases, handing its phosphoryl group to water. Under standard conditions, transfers run downhill. ATP sits in the middle. Compounds above it can recharge ADP. ATP, in turn, phosphorylates compounds below it.

scenes.tts: That middle seat is what makes A T P good currency. It can be refilled from above, and it can pay for jobs below. Here is the idea to hold. A T P is cash, not savings: spent on the cell's work, and remade by burning fuel.
scenes.caption: That middle seat is what makes ATP good currency. It can be refilled from above, and it can pay for jobs below. Here is the idea to hold. ATP is cash, not savings: spent on the cell's work, and remade by burning fuel.
scenes.visual: The middle terrace and its tray glow YELLOW; arrows into it from above and out of it below pulse in turn on 'refilled from above' and 'pay for jobs below'. On 'the cell's work', three small TEXT icons along the bottom terrace light in turn, labelled 'move', 'pump', 'build'. On 'burning fuel', an empty lift shaft labelled 'fuel' appears at the left edge of the terraces, reaching from the bottom to the middle terrace, with a faint ORANGE glow at its base. Large white line across the top during the last sentence: 'ATP: cash, not savings'.
scenes.narration: That middle seat is what makes ATP good currency. It can be refilled from above, and it can pay for jobs below. Here is the idea to hold. ATP is cash, not savings: spent on the cell's work, and remade by burning fuel.

scenes.tts: Now the remaking. The cell refills A T P by oxidizing fuel, in three stages. Digestion breaks a steak, a potato and olive oil into amino acids, sugars and fatty acids. Most of their carbon then funnels into one molecule, acetyl co A. Different highways, one city center.
scenes.caption: Now the remaking. The cell refills ATP by oxidizing fuel, in three stages. Digestion breaks a steak, a potato and olive oil into amino acids, sugars and fatty acids. Most of their carbon then funnels into one molecule, acetyl-CoA. Different highways, one city center.
scenes.visual: Pan left so the fuel lift fills about 60% of the frame, terraces still visible at right. Three labelled icons sit at the top left: 'steak', 'potato', 'olive oil'. On 'Digestion', each breaks into a stream of small BLUE beads relabelled 'amino acids', 'sugars', 'fatty acids'. On 'funnels', the three streams curve together like roads merging into one central plaza, a large GOLD-outlined block labelled 'acetyl-CoA'; one thin dashed amino-acid stream peels off and enters lower down, tagged 'some enter elsewhere'. The streams keep flowing through the city-center sentence.
scenes.narration: Now the remaking. The cell refills ATP by oxidizing fuel, in three stages. Digestion breaks a steak, a potato and olive oil into amino acids, sugars and fatty acids. Most of their carbon then funnels into one molecule, acetyl-CoA. Different highways, one city center.

scenes.tts: The citric acid cycle oxidizes acetyl co A to carbon dioxide. The electrons it strips away load onto carriers, N A D H and F A D H two. Handing those electrons on to oxygen drives A T P synthesis.
scenes.caption: The citric acid cycle oxidizes acetyl-CoA to carbon dioxide. The electrons it strips away load onto carriers, NADH and FADH₂. Handing those electrons on to oxygen drives ATP synthesis.
scenes.visual: The acetyl-CoA block feeds a large slowly turning wheel labelled 'citric acid cycle'. As it turns, two small grey 'CO₂' puffs drift off the top, and TEAL electron sparks jump from the wheel into YELLOW trucks labelled 'NADH' and 'FADH₂'. On 'handed to oxygen', the trucks drive to a block labelled 'O₂' at the base of the fuel lift and drop their TEAL sparks into it; the lift starts to run, raising dim 'ADP' beads to the middle terrace, where they brighten to YELLOW 'ATP' and drop into the tray. The lift keeps running.
scenes.narration: The citric acid cycle oxidizes acetyl-CoA to carbon dioxide. The electrons it strips away load onto carriers, NADH and FADH₂. Handing those electrons on to oxygen drives ATP synthesis.

scenes.tts: So burning a fuel means stripping electrons from its carbons. Here is a test. Take one carbon from a fatty acid's long chain, and one carbon from glucose. Which one has more electrons to give?
scenes.caption: So burning a fuel means stripping electrons from its carbons. Here is a test. Take one carbon from a fatty acid's long chain, and one carbon from glucose. Which one has more electrons to give?
scenes.visual: Two large BLUE carbon tokens rise beside the wheel, side by side: left labelled 'fatty acid carbon', right labelled 'glucose carbon'. Each has an empty TEAL spark meter beneath it, outcome not yet shown. On the final question, large white text across the top: 'Which carbon has more to give?' The wheel and lift keep turning slowly behind.
scenes.narration: So burning a fuel means stripping electrons from its carbons. Here is a test. Take one carbon from a fatty acid's long chain, and one carbon from glucose. Which one has more electrons to give?

scenes.visual: Hold 'Which carbon has more to give?' for 4.5 seconds over the two tokens. A four-dot thinking indicator fills one dot per second; the two empty meters flicker faintly; nothing is revealed.

scenes.tts: The fatty acid's. Its carbons are loaded with hydrogens, so they have many electrons to give. Every carbon in glucose is already bonded to oxygen, so it has fewer. That is the main reason fat yields about nine kilocalories per gram, and carbohydrate about four.
scenes.caption: The fatty acid's. Its carbons are loaded with hydrogens, so they have many electrons to give. Every carbon in glucose is already bonded to oxygen, so it has fewer. That is the main reason fat yields about 9 kcal per gram, and carbohydrate about 4.
scenes.visual: On 'loaded with hydrogens', small white 'H' tags cluster around the fatty-acid token and its TEAL meter fills high. On 'bonded to oxygen', a RED 'O' tag attaches to the glucose token and its meter fills only partway. On 'nine kilocalories', two bars rise under the tokens, drawn to the lesson's values: 'fat ~9 kcal/g' and 'carbohydrate ~4 kcal/g', the fat bar 2.25 times the carbohydrate bar. TEAL sparks keep streaming from both tokens onto the YELLOW carrier trucks.
scenes.narration: The fatty acid's. Its carbons are loaded with hydrogens, so they have many electrons to give. Every carbon in glucose is already bonded to oxygen, so it has fewer. That is the main reason fat yields about 9 kcal per gram, and carbohydrate about 4.

scenes.tts: So the body keeps two accounts. Fat is its main long-term store, the savings. A T P is the small pool of cash, emptied and refilled all day. Work keeps spending it, and burning fuel keeps paying it back.
scenes.caption: So the body keeps two accounts. Fat is its main long-term store, the savings. ATP is the small pool of cash, emptied and refilled all day. Work keeps spending it, and burning fuel keeps paying it back.
scenes.visual: Pull back to the whole world: fuel lift at left, terraces at right, tray on the middle terrace. On 'Fat', a large BLUE-outlined vault labelled 'fat: long-term store' settles at the bottom left beside the fuel streams. On 'small pool of cash', the tray with its four YELLOW beads glows, still tagged 'under 1 kg'. On the last sentence, beads flow out of the tray to the 'move', 'pump', 'build' icons and back up the running lift, a continuous loop.
scenes.narration: So the body keeps two accounts. Fat is its main long-term store, the savings. ATP is the small pool of cash, emptied and refilled all day. Work keeps spending it, and burning fuel keeps paying it back.

scenes.visual: End card over the dimmed but still moving world (YELLOW beads looping from tray to work icons and back up the fuel lift). Large white text, centred: 'ATP is cash, not savings: spent by work, remade by fuel.' The site mascot Hex waves twice below it.
